toc.title: A CI workflow: build and test on every change
Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue

html:
1A CI workflow: build and test on every change

Continuous integration (CI) means that every push and pull request is built and tested automatically, so a broken change shows up before it is merged. The figure shows the pipeline from a push to a green or red check.

A CI job has the same shape for every language: get the code, set up the language, install, test.

# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with: {node-version: 22, cache: npm}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
Step Node project Python project
Set up actions/setup-node@v7 with node-version actions/setup-python@v5 with python-version
Cache cache: npm cache: pip
Install npm ci pip install -r requirements.txt
Test npm test python -m unittest

Action versions move on. The ones above are the major versions in the official examples when this course was written, so check each action's releases page before you copy one.

Tip

. Quote Python versions in YAML. An unquoted 3.10 is read as the number 3.1, so the job would install the wrong Python.

2Matrix, cache and artifacts

A matrix runs one job definition many times with different values, for example two operating systems and two Python versions.

Key Effect
matrix Every combination of the listed values becomes its own job
exclude Removes one combination
include Adds one more combination, for example macOS with Python 3.13
fail-fast True by default: the first failure cancels the other jobs; false lets all finish
max-parallel Limits how many matrix jobs run at once 
# .github/workflows/matrix.yml
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]
        python: ["3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude: [{os: windows-latest, python: "3.12"}]
    steps: [{uses: actions/setup-python@v5, with: {python-version: "${{ matrix.python }}"}}]

Two operating systems times two versions gives four combinations. The exclude removes one, so three jobs run.

Caching saves the time of downloading dependencies again. The easy way is cache: npm or cache: pip in the setup action. By hand, use actions/cache with a path, a key of at most 512 characters and optional restore-keys.

Cache fact Detail
Hit The exact key was found, and the step output cache-hit is true
Immutable A cache never changes; to refresh it, change the key, for example with a hash of the lock file
Eviction Entries not used for 7 days are removed; the default limit is 10 GB per repository
Scope Per branch: a pull request uses the merge ref, and sibling branches cannot share

An artifact is different: it moves files out of a job, to a later job or to a person. Upload with actions/upload-artifact (name, path, retention-days) and download with actions/download-artifact. Jobs run on separate machines, so the consuming job must list the producer in needs. Version 4 artifacts are immutable, and they share storage with Packages.

# .github/workflows/artifact.yml
on: push
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: mkdir dist; echo shop > dist/a.txt
      - {uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4, with: {name: site, path: dist}}
  check:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps: [{uses: actions/download-artifact@v5, with: {name: site}}]
Tip

. Never make a build depend on a cache hit. A cache is a speed-up that can be missing; an artifact is the result of this run.

3Secrets, variables and environments

Repository secrets are saved in Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. Organizations can hold secrets too, and so can an environment: a named target such as staging or production that a job selects with environment:.

Item How a workflow reads it Rules
Secret ${{ secrets.NAME }} in with or env Never on the command line; an unset secret is an empty string
Variable ${{ vars.NAME }} Plain configuration, not for secrets
GITHUB_TOKEN ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} Made for each job; ends when the job ends

Secrets are not given to workflows triggered from forks (only the read-only token is) or by Dependabot. A secret also cannot be used directly in an if:. Copy it into a job-level env: variable and test that variable instead, as the called workflow in section 5 does.

Tip

. To test whether a secret exists, put it in a job-level env: and write if: env.TOKEN != ''. A condition that names secrets.TOKEN directly does not work.

4Permissions, concurrency, filters and the merge queue

Permissions. Set permissions to limit what GITHUB_TOKEN can do: read, write or none for each scope, such as contents. If you set any scope, every scope you leave out becomes none. The shorthands are read-all, write-all and {} (nothing). Use least privilege: read contents at the top of the file and raise one job only when it needs more.

Setting What it does
concurrency group Only one run per group at a time, for example one per branch
cancel-in-progress Off by default; true cancels the running run when a newer one starts
paths, paths-ignore Run only when the changed files match (a skipped required check stays Pending)
merge_group The event of a merge queue; type checks_requested

A merge queue merges pull requests into a busy protected branch in order. Each pull request is tested against the latest target branch plus the pull requests queued before it. If a required check must run for the queue, its workflow must also listen to merge_group.

Tip

. Set cancel-in-progress: true on a branch group. Three quick pushes then cost one finished run instead of three.

5Reusable workflows

A reusable workflow is a workflow other workflows can call. The called file sits in .github/workflows and starts with on: workflow_call, which can declare inputs (boolean, number or string), secrets and outputs.

# .github/workflows/deploy.yml
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs: {target: {type: string, default: staging}}
    secrets: {token: {required: true}}
    outputs: {url: {value: "${{ jobs.run.outputs.url }}"}}
jobs:
  run:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs: {url: "${{ steps.d.outputs.url }}"}
    env: {TOKEN: "${{ secrets.token }}", T: "${{ inputs.target }}"}
    steps: [{id: d, if: "env.TOKEN != ''", run: 'echo "url=https://example.test/$T" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"'}]

The caller uses the file at job level with uses, not as a step, and hands over with: and secrets: (or secrets: inherit inside one organization or enterprise).

# .github/workflows/release.yml
on:
  push: {branches: [main], paths: ["src/**"]}
  merge_group:
permissions: {contents: read}
concurrency: {group: "deploy-${{ github.ref }}", cancel-in-progress: true}
jobs:
  stage:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml
    with: {target: staging}
    secrets: {token: "${{ secrets.DEPLOY_TOKEN }}"}
  report: {needs: stage, runs-on: ubuntu-latest, steps: [{run: "echo $URL", env: {URL: "${{ needs.stage.outputs.url }}"}}]}
Rule Detail
Path forms ./.github/workflows/file.yml or owner/repo/.github/workflows/file.yml@ref; a commit SHA is safest
Nesting Up to 10 levels
Permissions A called workflow can keep or lower them, never raise them

6Practice Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A matrix has os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] and python: ["3.12", "3.13"], plus one exclude for Windows with 3.12. How many jobs run?

  • AFour, because an exclude entry only works together with include
  • BTwo, because matrix keys are used one at a time, not combined
  • CThree, because exclude removes one of four combinations
  • DFive, because exclude also adds one combination to the matrix
Show the answer

Answer: C. The matrix makes four combinations and the exclude entry removes one of them.

S2A cache step uses the fixed key npm-cache. The lock file changed, but the install still shows the old packages. Why?

  • ACaches expire at once when the lock file is edited
  • BCaches are immutable, so the same key restores old files
  • CThe restore-keys setting blocks every newer cache entry
  • DCache entries can be read only by the sibling branches
Show the answer

Answer: B. Caches are immutable, so a new key (for example with a hash of the lock file) is needed to refresh one.

S3A step has if: secrets.TOKEN != '', and the run reports an error. What is the correct fix?

  • AQuote the whole condition so that it reads as plain text
  • BMove the secret into the with: block of the same step
  • CCreate the secret again as a plain repository variable
  • DCopy it into a job-level env variable and test that
Show the answer

Answer: D. A secret cannot be used directly in an if:, but a job-level env variable that holds it can.

S4A workflow sets only permissions: contents: read at the top. A step then tries to comment on a pull request with the token and is refused. Why?

  • ASetting any scope turns every unlisted scope to none
  • BThe read value also blocks writes to the contents scope
  • CComments are not allowed for workflows run by a push
  • DThe token ends when the first job of the run is done
Show the answer

Answer: A. Once one scope is set, every scope that is left out becomes none, so the job needs pull-requests: write.

S5Three pushes in a minute start three CI runs on one branch, and only the last one matters. What should you add?

  • AA needs key that makes each run wait for the older one
  • BA concurrency group per branch with cancel-in-progress: true
  • CA max-parallel value of one in the matrix strategy
  • DA paths filter that skips runs for repeated pushes
Show the answer

Answer: B. Concurrency allows one run per group, and cancel-in-progress stops the older run when a newer one starts.

S6A caller workflow has - uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml as a step, and the run fails. What is the fix?

  • AAdd on: workflow_dispatch to the called workflow file
  • BRename the called file so that it ends with .yaml
  • CCopy the called file into the actions folder instead
  • DMove uses to the job level, as in jobs.stage.uses
Show the answer

Answer: D. A reusable workflow is called with uses on the job, never as a step.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the default of fail-fast in a matrix?

Show the answer

True: the first failure cancels the other jobs.

R2How long can a cache entry go unused before it is evicted?

Show the answer

7 days.

R3Which key must a job add to use an artifact made by another job?

Show the answer

needs, naming the producer job.

R4Which trigger declares a reusable workflow?

Show the answer

on: workflow_call.

R5Which event must a workflow listen to so its checks run in a merge queue?

Show the answer

merge_group.

R6What does permissions: {} do?

Show the answer

It gives the token no permissions at all.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
CI job checkout, set up the language, install, test; cache: npm or cache: pip
Matrix matrix makes combinations; exclude removes, include adds; fail-fast true by default
Cache key up to 512 characters; immutable; evicted after 7 days; 10 GB per repository
Artifacts upload-artifact and download-artifact; the consumer needs the producer
Secrets secrets.NAME in with or env; never directly in if:; none for forks
Permissions set one scope and the rest become none; start with read contents
Concurrency group plus cancel-in-progress (off by default)
Reuse workflow_call with inputs, secrets, outputs; caller uses uses at job level
